sources.outlet: U.S. Senate roll call vote 118, 119th Congress 2nd session
sources.searcher_note: Primary record: motion to discharge S.J.Res.163 (Iran war powers) rejected 49 yea, 50 nay, 1 not voting (Ricketts R-NE); Fetterman (D-PA) voted Nay.

sources.quote: Democrat John Fetterman of Pennsylvania voted no, lining up with most Republicans against his own party's effort.
sources.searcher_note: June 16 vote on S.J.Res.172 (Warnock) 'went down 47-48'; five sat out: Bennet, Booker, Hawley, McConnell, Sanders. Matches the lead's second one-vote failure, and names Hawley and McConnell as absent too.

sources.quote: Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman broke ranks with Democrats to oppose the resolution, while Republican Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky voted in support of the measure.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found: first Iran war-powers vote (Kaine), failed 47-53, Fetterman the Democratic defector.

sources.quote: Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania was the sole Democrat to oppose.
sources.searcher_note: Eighth vote: Senate advanced a war-powers resolution 50-47 for the first time (Cornyn, Tuberville, Tillis absent); Fetterman again the only Democrat opposed.

sources.quote: Republican Sens. Lisa Murkowski, Susan Collins, Rand Paul and Thom Tillis joined all but one Democrat, Sen. John Fetterman, in voting in favor of the resolution.
sources.searcher_note: Recent (post-2026-06-30): 2026-09-24 vote failed 49-50 with Fetterman the lone Democrat against; says the Senate has voted on Iran war powers 14 times and passed it once (late June, McConnell and McCormick absent).

sources.quote: On May 13th, Republicans blocked Senator Merkley's (D-OR) resolution 49-50.
sources.searcher_note: Dated list of every blocked vote: Mar 4, 18, 24; Apr 15, 22, 30; May 13 (49-50); Jun 16 (47-48); Jun 24; Jul 23; Jul 30 (49-50); Sep 24 (49-50). Does not name Fetterman.

notes: Fetterman being the only Democrat siding with Republicans is reported vote by vote (Mar 4, May 19, Jun 16, Sep 24, plus Democracy Now 2026-07-31 on a 50-49 vote). No source found that tallies his record as 'all 12' votes through 2026-06-24, or that pairs the May 13 and June 16 one-vote failures. Vote counts differ by source: ABC says 14 Senate votes by 2026-09-24 with one passage (late June); CBS 2026-05-19 says a discharge motion passed 50-47; the Democrats' list shows 9 blocked votes through June 24. Later one-vote failures on Jul 30 and Sep 24 (both 49-50) are covered widely, after the lead's table cutoff. NPR 2026-09-24 timed out; CNN 2026-06-24 ('Senate votes to walk back rebuke of Trump over Iran') returned 451; a Yahoo March article returned 404. No source disagreeing with the Fetterman finding found.
